biological.citation: LRP1 is a neuronal receptor for α-synuclein uptake and spread (PMID: 36056345)
biological.summary: LRP1 knockout in human iPSC-derived neurons significantly reduced uptake of monomeric and oligomeric α-synuclein, and to a lesser extent pre-formed fibrils. The N-terminus and lysine residues of α-synuclein were critical for LRP1-mediated internalization. In a neuronal Lrp1 conditional knockout mouse model, spread of α-synuclein in the hippocampus was significantly reduced compared to wild-type littermates.

biological.citation: Astrocytic LRP1 enables mitochondria transfer to neurons and mitigates brain ischemic stroke by suppressing ARF1 lactylation (PMID: 38906140)
biological.summary: Astrocytic LRP1 suppresses glucose uptake, glycolysis, and lactate production, thereby reducing lactylation of ARF1 and promoting astrocyte-to-neuron mitochondria transfer. Suppression of astrocytic LRP1 in a mouse ischemia-reperfusion model worsened stroke injury and reduced mitochondria transfer to damaged neurons. CSF lactate was elevated in human stroke patients and inversely correlated with astrocytic mitochondria levels.

biological.citation: Low-density-lipoprotein-receptor-related protein 1 mediates Notch pathway activation (PMID: 34626540)
biological.summary: LRP1 was identified as a key regulator of the Notch signaling pathway through a protein interaction landscape analysis. LRP1 mediates ubiquitination chain linkage switching of Delta ligands, affecting ligand recycling, membrane localization, and stability. LRP1 inhibition led to Notch signaling inhibition and decreased tumorigenesis in leukemia cell models.

biological.citation: Heterozygous LRP1 deficiency causes developmental dysplasia of the hip by impairing triradiate chondrocytes differentiation due to inhibition of autophagy (PMID: 36067312)
biological.summary: Whole-exome sequencing identified likely pathogenic LRP1 variants in two DDH families and seven sporadic patients. Heterozygous Lrp1 knockout mice and Lrp1 knockin mice with a human DDH-associated missense variant (R1783W) recapitulated DDH phenotypes. Mechanistically, Lrp1 deficiency impaired chondrogenic differentiation by decreasing autophagy and upregulating β-catenin signaling.

biological.citation: Skeletal progenitor LRP1 deficiency causes severe and persistent skeletal defects with Wnt pathway dysregulation (PMID: 39865089)
biological.summary: LRP1 is abundantly expressed in skeletal progenitor cells from mouse embryonic stage E10.5, especially in the perichondrium. Lrp1 deficiency in skeletal progenitors caused joint fusion, cartilage/bone malformation, and severe skeletal defects resembling Wnt signaling pathway phenotypes. LRP1 directly binds Wnt5a, facilitates its endocytic degradation and recycling, and regulates non-canonical Wnt/PCP components Wnt5a and Vangl2 in developing limbs.

biological.citation: LRP1 Repression by SNAIL Results in ECM Remodeling in Genetic Risk for Vascular Diseases (PMID: 39355906)
biological.summary: Multitrait colocalization analyses identified rs11172113 as the most likely causal variant at the LRP1 locus for fibromuscular dysplasia, migraine, pulse pressure, and spontaneous coronary artery dissection, with the T allele associated with higher LRP1 expression. In iPSC-derived smooth muscle cells, LRP1 knockout decreased proliferation and migration, enhanced TGF-β/SMAD2/3 signaling, and remodeled the extracellular matrix. The transcription factor SNAIL was found to repress LRP1 expression through an allele-specific mechanism involving the disease risk allele.

biological.citation: Genome-wide CRISPR screening identifies LRP1 as an entry factor for SFTSV (PMID: 40301361)
biological.summary: A genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen identified LRP1 as a host entry factor for Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Virus (SFTSV). Knockdown or knockout of LRP1 significantly attenuated SFTSV infection in mouse embryonic fibroblasts, and co-IP and surface plasmon resonance revealed direct interaction between SFTSV glycoprotein Gn and LRP1 via CLI and CLII domains. LRP1 antagonists and neutralizing antibodies reduced viral load and improved survival in a lethal mouse model.

biological.citation: Schwann cell LRP1 regulates remak bundle ultrastructure and axonal interactions to prevent neuropathic pain (PMID: 23536074)
biological.summary: LRP1 is expressed in Schwann cells of the peripheral nervous system, where it is essential for normal axon myelination and ensheathment of axons in Remak bundles. Schwann cell-specific LRP1 deletion (scLRP1-/-) in mice caused mechanical allodynia even without nerve injury, accelerated degeneration after crush injury, and impaired remyelination. Central sensitization markers including p38MAPK activation and microglial activation were elevated in the spinal cord of scLRP1-/- mice.

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Regulation of HDL-c levels via ABCA1: A role for LRP1 (ASHG 2016)
biological.summary: Two missense mutations in LRP1 (p.Val3244Ile and p.Glu3983Asp) were identified in individuals with extremely low HDL-c levels, and the LRP1 locus was strongly associated with HDL-c and ApoA1 levels in a large Danish cohort. Mutant LRP1 proteins were reduced by 40-60% in stability, and ABCA1 cell surface localization was decreased by 60-70% in carrier fibroblasts and LRP1-deficient cells. LRP1 was found to regulate intracellular trafficking of ABCA1 to the plasma membrane via modulation of lysosomal enzyme Cathepsin D and Prosaposin levels.

biological.citation: Meta-analysis of genome-wide association data of 20,000 migraine cases identifies two novel gene loci and supports several biologically relevant mechanisms (ASHG 2011)
biological.summary: A large-scale GWAS meta-analysis of approximately 20,000 migraine cases and 90,000 controls identified LRP1 (rs11172113 at 12q13.3) as one of the genome-wide significant loci associated with migraine susceptibility. This finding was replicated across multiple clinic- and population-based cohorts from three continents. Subsequent Bayesian conditional analysis further strengthened the LRP1 association signal (p-value improving from 3.94×10⁻¹⁹ to 1.41×10⁻²⁶) and identified multiple independent signals at this locus.
